Volumetric 3-component velocimetry measurements were taken of the flow field near a Rushton turbine in a stirred tank reactor.
The flow field was characterized by a strong radial jet, large tank-scale ring vortices, and small-scale blade tip vortices.
Approximately 15,000 3D velocity vectors were obtained in a cubic measurement volume.
Measurements were performed at three Reynolds numbers: 15,000, 107,000, and 137,000.

Three methods were used to identify the tip vortices: calculation of circumferential vorticity, calculation of local pressure minima via an eigenvalue approach ('λ2'), and calculation of swirling strength via an eigenvalue approach ('λci').
The 'swirl strength' criterion provided the clearest identification of the tip vortices.
Visualization of tip vortices up to 140 degrees past blade passage was observed in the highest Reynolds number case (137,000), which had not been previously shown.
The related article appears in the online first section of Experiments in Fluids (2009), doi 10.1007/s00348-009-0711-9.
The associated video can be viewed in MPEG-2 and MPEG-1 formats.
Rushton turbines are commonly used impellers in stirred tank reactors, which are widely used in chemical, biochemical, and pharmaceutical industries.
Understanding the complex, 3D flow field around a Rushton turbine is crucial for optimizing the design and operation of stirred tank reactors.
The volumetric nature of the data enabled tip vortex identification, vortex trajectory analysis, and calculation of vortex strength, providing the most comprehensive view of the flow field to date.
The study was a collaboration between researchers from Penn State University and TSI Incorporated.
The measurements were taken in a cubic volume, allowing for a detailed 3D characterization of the flow field.
The high-resolution data offers new insights into the complex flow dynamics around a Rushton turbine.
